zh.title: 美國空軍占地面積最大的七座基地 內利斯綜合設施達5000平方英里
zh.summary: 美國空軍七座占地面積最大的基地由小至大依序為費爾柴爾德、柯特蘭、愛德華茲、艾格林、希爾、巴里·戈德華特靶場與內利斯綜合設施，面積由21平方英里至5000平方英里不等，涵蓋空中加油、核武指揮、飛行測試、武器評估與實戰化訓練等任務。
body: 排名第七的費爾柴爾德空軍基地占地21平方英里，位於華盛頓州斯波坎西南方，是空中機動司令部的重要空中加油樞紐，駐紮的第92空中加油聯隊操作大批KC-135空中加油機；基地也是空軍唯一的求生、脫逃、抵抗與躲避（SERE）學校所在地，每年訓練約2萬名學員。排名第六的柯特蘭空軍基地占地68平方英里，是空軍全球打擊司令部核指揮與後勤部門的所在地，也是太空軍第15三角洲的總部，約有2萬名軍文職人員，基地內還有空軍研究實驗室定向能部門與太空載具部門，以及包括桑迪亞與洛斯阿拉莫斯國家實驗室在內的逾100個任務夥伴單位。排名第五的愛德華茲空軍基地占地469平方英里，位於南加州莫哈韋沙漠，駐有空軍試飛員學校、NASA阿姆斯壯飛行研究中心與空軍研究實驗室，也是空軍測試中心總部；羅傑斯乾湖床提供65平方英里的天然跑道，基地還擁有全球最大的無響室。耶格上尉1947年在此駕駛Bell X-1突破音障，此後F-117、F-22、F-35與B-2皆在此測試，B-21如今也在其空域飛行，NASA與洛克希德合作的X-59靜音超音速技術驗證機則於2025年10月底首飛。

排名第四的艾格林空軍基地占地724平方英里，位於佛羅里達州狹長地帶，是美國空軍武器、導航與導引系統的主要測試評估中心，駐有近2萬名軍方、文職與承包商人員；第33戰鬥機聯隊在此負責F-35A飛行員與維修人員的聯合訓練，基地還管理延伸至墨西哥灣的大片海上靶場，並設有麥金利氣候實驗室與空軍研究實驗室彈藥部門。排名第三的希爾空軍基地占地2657平方英里，管理面積1490平方英里的猶他測試與訓練靶場，駐有空軍首支成軍的F-35戰鬥機聯隊第388聯隊；奧格登航空後勤綜合體負責F-22、F-35、F-16、C-130、A-10與民兵三型洲際彈道飛彈的全壽期維持，基地約有2萬名軍文職人員。

排名第二的巴里·戈德華特空軍靶場占地2969平方英里，是美軍首要的軍事訓練靶場之一，可進行實彈空對空與空對地戰術訓練，靶場相關基地約有1.5萬名人員，由路克空軍基地與尤馬海軍陸戰隊航空站共同管理；路克空軍基地是空軍主要的戰鬥機飛行員訓練基地，也是F-35A的主要訓練中心，駐紮的第56戰鬥機聯隊是美國空軍最大的戰鬥機聯隊。排名第一的內利斯空軍基地綜合設施占地5000平方英里，主設施位於拉斯維加斯谷地東北角，駐有1.5萬名軍文職人員，每年舉辦紅旗演習，駐有空軍作戰中心、第99空軍基地聯隊與雷鳥飛行表演隊；綜合設施涵蓋內華達測試與訓練靶場、克里奇空軍基地與托諾帕測試靶場，靶場約有300萬英畝的限制空域與土地，包括著名的51區，U-2、SR-71與F-117皆在此研發，桑迪亞國家實驗室亦位於托諾帕測試靶場範圍內。

en.title: The 7 largest US Air Force bases by land area
en.summary: The seven largest US Air Force bases by land area, smallest to largest, are Fairchild, Kirtland, Edwards, Eglin, Hill, the Barry M. Goldwater Range and the Nellis complex, ranging from 21 to 5,000 square miles and covering aerial refuelling, nuclear command, flight testing, weapons evaluation and combat training.
body: Seventh is Fairchild Air Force Base at 21 square miles, just southwest of Spokane, Washington. The base is a critical component of Air Mobility Command and serves as one of the largest aerial refuelling hubs in the USAF, with the host 92nd Air Refueling Wing operating a large fleet of KC-135 Stratotanker aircraft. It is also home to the Air Force's only Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape School, which trains roughly 20,000 students annually. Sixth is Kirtland Air Force Base at 68 square miles, home to the nuclear command and logistics arm of Air Force Global Strike Command. The Space Force's Delta 15 is headquartered at Kirtland, and the base is one of the largest employment sources in New Mexico, with 20,000 personnel including troops and civilians. It also hosts the Air Force Research Laboratory Directed Energy Directorate and the Space Vehicles Directorate, and supports over 100 mission partners and units, including the Department of Energy's Sandia National Laboratories and Los Alamos National Laboratory. Fifth is Edwards Air Force Base at 469 square miles, deep in the Mojave Desert of Southern California, home to the US Air Force Test Pilot School as well as NASA's Armstrong Flight Research Center and the Air Force Research Laboratory. Edwards is the headquarters for the Air Force Test Center. The bed of Rogers Dry Lake provides a 65-square-mile natural runway, and the base has the largest anechoic chamber in the world for testing aircraft electronic and radio frequency systems. Air Force Captain Chuck Yeager was the first human being to break the sound barrier when he flew the Bell X-1 rocket plane over the speed of sound at Edwards in 1947. The F-117 Nighthawk, F-22 Raptor, F-35 Lightning II and B-2 Spirit were all tested there, and the B-21 Raider is now flying over its airfield. NASA and Lockheed are testing the X-59 QueSST at Edwards, which took its first flight at the end of October 2025.

Fourth is Eglin Air Force Base at 724 square miles, in the northwest corner of Florida, the primary test and evaluation center for all USAF weapons, navigation, and guidance systems. The installation hosts almost 20,000 military, civilian, and contractor personnel from the Air Force, Army, and Navy. The 33rd Fighter Wing is a joint training unit for both pilots and maintainers of the F-35A Lightning II. To facilitate its weapons-centric mission, the base manages a vast overwater range extending into the Gulf of Mexico, and the McKinley Climatic Laboratory tests aircraft under severe weather conditions. Third is Hill Air Force Base at 2,657 square miles, which manages the Utah Test and Training Range, a 1,490-square-mile expanse of desert used for testing and tactical training. Hill is home to the first F-35 fighter wing that became operational in the USAF, the 388th Fighter Wing, and the Ogden Air Logistics Complex manages the life cycle sustainment of the F-22 Raptor, F-35 Lightning II, F-16 Fighting Falcon, C-130 Hercules, and A-10 Thunderbolt II, as well as the Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile. As many as 20,000 troops and civilians work on the base.

Second is the Barry M. Goldwater Air Force Range at 2,969 square miles, one of the premier military training ranges in the United States, used for realistic combat training with extensive live-fire air-to-air and air-to-ground tactical training. Around 15,000 people work at the range and the bases associated with it. The range is jointly managed by Luke Air Force Base and Marine Corps Air Station Yuma. Luke is the primary fighter pilot training facility in the US Air Force and the main training center for the F-35A Lightning II, and the 56th Fighter Wing based there is the largest fighter wing in the USAF. First is the Nellis Air Force Base Complex at 5,000 square miles. Its main facility is situated in the northeastern corner of the Las Vegas Valley, hosting 15,000 troops and civilian staff, and every year the international air warfare exercise known as Red Flag is held at Nellis. The airfield is home to the Air Force Warfare Center as well as the 99th Air Base Wing and the aerial demonstration team known as the Thunderbirds. The complex includes the Nevada Test and Training Range, Creech Air Force Base, and the Tonopah Test Range. The NTTR encompasses approximately 3 million acres of restricted airspace and land, which is home to the famed, highly classified Area 51, as well as the Tonopah Test Range. These facilities were instrumental in the development of the Lockheed U-2 Dragon Lady, SR-71 Blackbird, and F-117 Nighthawk, and Sandia National Laboratories is also located on the base complex, within the boundaries of the Tonopah Test Range.

facts.claim: Fairchild AFB covers 21 square miles southwest of Spokane, Washington, is an Air Mobility Command aerial refuelling hub, hosts the 92nd Air Refueling Wing operating KC-135 Stratotankers, and is home to the Air Force's only SERE School, training roughly 20,000 students a year.

Kirtland AFB covers 68 square miles, hosts the nuclear command and logistics arm of Air Force Global Strike Command and the Space Force's Delta 15 headquarters, employs 20,000 personnel, and supports over 100 mission partners including Sandia and Los Alamos National Laboratories.

Edwards AFB covers 469 square miles in the Mojave Desert, hosts the USAF Test Pilot School, NASA's Armstrong Flight Research Center and the Air Force Test Center, has a 65-square-mile natural runway on Rogers Dry Lake and the world's largest anechoic chamber, and is where Chuck Yeager broke the sound barrier in the Bell X-1 in 1947.
The F-117, F-22, F-35 and B-2 were tested at Edwards, the B-21 is now flying over its airfield, and the X-59 QueSST took its first flight at the end of October 2025.

Eglin AFB covers 724 square miles in the Florida Panhandle, is the primary test and evaluation center for USAF weapons, navigation and guidance systems, hosts almost 20,000 personnel and the 33rd Fighter Wing joint F-35A training unit, and manages an overwater range in the Gulf of Mexico.

Hill AFB covers 2,657 square miles, manages the 1,490-square-mile Utah Test and Training Range, is home to the first operational F-35 wing (388th Fighter Wing), and its Ogden Air Logistics Complex sustains the F-22, F-35, F-16, C-130 and A-10 plus the Minuteman III missile.

The Barry M. Goldwater Range covers 2,969 square miles, is used for live-fire air-to-air and air-to-ground tactical training with around 15,000 people at the range and associated bases, is jointly managed by Luke AFB and MCAS Yuma, and Luke's 56th Fighter Wing is the largest fighter wing in the USAF.

The Nellis AFB Complex covers 5,000 square miles, hosts 15,000 troops and civilians, holds the annual Red Flag exercise, the Air Force Warfare Center, the 99th Air Base Wing and the Thunderbirds, and includes the Nevada Test and Training Range, Creech AFB and the Tonopah Test Range, with about 3 million acres of restricted airspace and land including Area 51.
